notes: Assertions are at the prompt-assembly level: attack content must arrive inside the untrusted delimiters as data, the system prompt must carry the data-is-not-instructions rule, and embedded END markers must be defused. Model-behavior grading (does a live model obey an injection despite the defense) is a separate, non-CI evaluation; the enforcement layer behind the prompt (plan allowlist, HITL trade approval) is covered by its own tests.
provenance: Synthetic red-team fixtures for the email-to-NLQ prompt-injection defense (RSI-InfoSec #764, AISecOps #767, eval set #863). NOT production emails; they exist to exercise the defended prompt assembly deterministically in CI.
runner: tests/nlq_injection_evalset.test.ts — assembles each case through the production plannerPrompt/withUntrustedRule helpers (src/agents/nlq/llmPlanning.ts, #862) and asserts the separation invariants per case, plus a negative control (the undefended assembly must fail the same invariants).
